newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London down on weaker dollar.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London down on weaker dollar.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London edged lower in quiet trade on Monday, weighed down by profit-taking in bank issues and selling in exporter shares on the back of a weaker U.S. dollar, traders said.

The Nikkei 50 index of leading shares traded in London edged some 14.39 points or 0.99 percent below London's Friday close by 1545 GMT, after the Tokyo Nikkei 225 index ended some 137.55 points or 0.72 percent lower.
"It's been a very quiet day," one trader said, "There was interest overnight in banks, but it looks like people have given up on that theme."
Banks hit by profit-taking included Fuji Bank Ltd, which traded at 1,520 yen versus 1,570 yen at the Tokyo close. Sumitomo Bank Ltd was standing at 1,617.5 after 1,630 in Tokyo.
A weaker U.S. currency, which dipped below 123 yen, provoked selling in dollar-sensitive issues including Honda, which traded at 3,620 yen from Tokyo's 3,660 yen.
